cases.name: non_tail_call_self_recursive
cases.module: export function sumTo(n) { if (n) { return n + sumTo(n - 1); } return 0; }
cases.note:
Self-recursive *non-tail* call (`FastValKind::Call`, not `ReturnCall`):
`n` is used again after the recursive call returns (`n + sumTo(n - 1)`), so
it must survive the callee clobbering the register file. Exercises the
MiniBC call-stack machinery added for task #8: `StdExtOp::Call` (push a
return address, unlike `TailCall`'s pure pc-rewrite) + `MiniOp::Push`/`Pop`
(save/restore live-across-call registers) + a pop-and-resume `Return`, in
both the Rust interpreter (`MiniInterp::run`'s call_stack) and the
`minibc_c` backend's hand-written ext-op dispatch loop
(`run_minibc_c_func` in this file) + `dreamcompiler-minibc-c-interp`'s
`MiniBc::Push`/`Pop` opcode table entries. See
`dreamcompiler-mini-target/src/lower/block.rs`'s `FastValKind::Call` arm
and `dreamcompiler-compile/tests/corpus.rs`'s `corpus_non_tail_call` for
the lower-level (non-e2e) regression tests.

No `cps`/`cps_c`/`cps_rust`/`native_c`: all route through the *legacy*
`ContinuationConverter` (`to_cps/fast.rs`), which panics on this
*self*-recursive non-tail-call shape specifically (a genuinely different
call target than the caller works fine, per `non_tail_call_two_saved`
below) with `index out of bounds: the len is 6 but the index is 6` at
`to_cps/fast.rs:2574` — discovered by this test, not investigated further
for the same reason as the other documented legacy-path bugs in this file
(slated for removal in favor of `drive`, not worth fixing).

No `native_table_inlined`: genuinely hangs (confirmed via process CPU time,
not just slow) on this self-recursive shape — a separate, pre-existing bug
in the native-dispatch "inlined" call-promotion path, out of scope for
MiniBC lowering (task #8); not investigated further here.

cases.name: non_tail_call_two_saved
cases.module:
function addOne(x) { return x + 1; }
export function combine(a, b) { return addOne(a) + addOne(b); }
cases.effective_ts_group: fast_ir, minibc_c, native_table, native_table_inlined, cps, cps_c, cps_rust, native_c
cases.note:
Non-tail call to a *different* function (not self-recursive), with two
live-across-call values (`a` and `b`, saved/restored independently across
two separate calls). `(3+1)+(4+1)=9`. Unlike
`non_tail_call_self_recursive`, this shape does NOT trip the legacy
converter or the native_table_inlined hang -- both are specific to
self-recursion, not non-tail calls in general.

No `native_table_rust`: `dreamcompiler-cps-rust-backend`'s MultiCall
codegen generates a `(u64, u64)` tuple return type but then accesses it
with C-struct-style field syntax (`v_12.r0`/`.r1`, valid for
`dreamcompiler-cps-c-backend`'s generated structs but not Rust tuples,
which need `.0`/`.1`) -- a genuine, pre-existing bug in that backend's own
MultiCall lowering, discovered by this test (the first two-output MultiCall
case exercised through native_table_rust) and out of scope for MiniBC
lowering (task #8); not investigated further here.

Previously `ts_group` dropped `cps` for the TS-generated test: the TS
side's `"minibc-cps"` N-API target uses `compile_source_cps_minibc`'s
*`drive`* CPS conversion path, which had a genuine, confirmed bug on
exactly this "two independent calls to the same callee, combine results"
shape (computed `addOne(b)` alone, silently dropping `addOne(a)`'s
contribution) -- found via this family's own TS cross-interpreter test,
then reproduced in pure Rust and fixed via `to_cps.rs`'s
`remainder_forward`/`ContinuationOps::thread_extra` mechanism; see
`dreamcompiler-compile::tests::cps_drive_two_calls_to_same_callee_saved_across_second`.

cases.name: mask_low8
cases.module: export function maskLow8(x) { return x & 0xFF; }
cases.note:
D2 Step 4(B) narrowing: `x & 0xFF` -> Stage C (`reduce_bitwidth_fast`)
narrows the AND's width to 8 -> the Fast IR lowering emits a raw R1
BitwiseAnd whose result rests in a single 16-bit register, recanonicalised
to R4 before the return. Proves the narrowing path computes correctly
end-to-end (not just the bytecode shape). 0x1234 (4660) & 0xFF = 0x34 = 52.

cases.name: bor_neg
cases.module: export function bor(a, b) { return a | b; }
cases.note:
`|`/`^` rest in a raw signed R2 register (width 32) and widen back
sign-extended -- this case produces a *negative* ToInt32 result, so a wrong
(zero) widen would be caught.

cases.name: bxor_neg
cases.module: export function bxor(a, b) { return a ^ b; }
cases.note:
Same rationale as `bor_neg`, for `^`. (JS `~` is not lowered by the
frontend -- it becomes Poison -- so BitwiseNot narrowing is covered by a
mini-target unit test instead, not here.)

cases.name: mask_or_chain
cases.module: export function chain(x, y) { return (x & 0xFF) | (y & 0xFF); }
cases.note:
Raw bitwise chain: two unsigned R1 masked ANDs feed a (signed-form) R2 OR
without round-tripping through f64. 0x1234&0xFF=0x34, 0x5678&0xFF=0x78,
0x34|0x78=0x7C=124.

cases.name: shl_overflow
cases.module: export function shl(a, b) { return a << b; }
cases.note:
Shifts rest raw R2: `<<`/`>>` signed (sign-widen), `>>>` unsigned
(zero-widen). `1 << 31` overflows to the negative ToInt32 -2147483648.

cases.name: shr_neg
cases.module: export function shr(a, b) { return a >> b; }
cases.note: `-8 >> 1` = -4 (arithmetic shift).

cases.name: shru_unsigned
cases.module: export function shru(a, b) { return a >>> b; }
cases.note: `-1 >>> 0` = 4294967295 (logical/unsigned shift).

cases.name: e2e_inlineme
cases.note:
`outer(3, 4)` -> `7.0` -- Form B `inlineme` sentinel, inlined at call site.

Uses the canonical Form B pattern emitted by `portal-jsc-generator`. How it
works:

1. `func_expr` in `module/js.rs` handles `Expr::Bin { op: NullishCoalescing }`
   by recursing into the left operand. The left side is
   `globalThis['~Natives_inlineme']` which resolves to
   `MItem::Native("inlineme")`, so `inlineme` is stored as
   `MItem::Native("inlineme")` in the module's `funcs` map -- the
   `?? (function(){})` fallback is irrelevant at compile time and is dropped.

2. `is_inlinable` (Form B path) scans `inner`'s SSA for
   `Item::Call { callee: TCallee::Val(v) }` and follows the SSA chain of `v`
   through `Item::Just` nodes until it reaches
   `SValue::LoadId(inlineme_ident)`. It then calls `inbp.fetch` for
   `inlineme_ident` and finds `MItem::Native("inlineme")` -> returns `true`.

   The earlier (broken) implementation called `sfunc.cfg.def(LId::Id { id })`
   on an `SCfg` -- `def` exists only on `TCfg`. In SSA, `Item::Just { id }`
   holds an `SValueId` (not a `swc_ecma_ast::Id`), so the fix is to assign
   `cur = *id` directly.

3. `conv_block` detects the inlinable callee and splices `inner`'s body
   inline into `outer` rather than emitting a call, so `outer(3, 4)` -> `7.0`
   without any call overhead.

Form A (`globalThis['~Natives_inlineme']()` inline) still hangs inside SWC's
`Splatting::translate` and remains excluded -- see `parse_probe_inlineme_forms`
in pipeline.rs.

cases.name: e2e_inlineme_n
cases.note:
`outer(3, 4)` -> `7.0` via `inlineme_n` with upward propagation depth 1.

`inner` has `inlineme_n(1)`, which means:
  - `inner` is inlinable (depth = 1), so it is inlined into `middle`.
  - Because depth > 0, `middle` inherits inlinability with depth 0, so
    `middle` is also inlined into `outer`.
  - `outer` is a plain exported function and is compiled normally.

The final FastFunc for `outer` contains all arithmetic directly and the
interpreter should return `a + b = 7.0`.

cases.name: e2e_inlineme_n_param_depth
cases.note:
`outer(3, 4)` -> `7.0` where the `inlineme_n` depth argument is a *function
parameter* rather than a literal.

Exercises cross-frame constant propagation through `ParamEnv`: `inner` has
`inlineme_n(n)` where `n` is `inner`'s first parameter. `outer` calls
`inner(1, a, b)`, passing the literal `1` as `n`. `eval_const_int` must walk
from `inner`'s entry-block `Param(0)` up through the `CallSiteParamEnv` into
`outer`'s CFG to find the literal `1`, fold to `Some(1)`, and conclude `inner`
is inlinable with depth 1 (which also makes `middle` inlinable with depth 0).

cases.name: e2e_inlineme_n_stmt_call
cases.note:
`outer(3, 4)` -> `7.0` via propagation through a *stmt-level* (non-tail) call,
exercising the regular-`Item::Call` path in the propagated scan.

`inner` has `inlineme_n(1)`. `middle`'s stmt-level call to `inner` (`const r
= inner(a, b);`, not a tail call) should propagate depth 1 ->
`is_inlinable(middle)` returns `Some(0)`, so `middle` is inlined into
`outer`. `inner` is inlined into `middle` (now inline in `outer`). Final
result: `a + b`.

cases.name: e2e_inlineme_n_multi
cases.note:
`outer(3, 4)` -> `19.0` -- two callees with *different* `inlineme_n` depths
in the same function, exercising the `max` over all call-site results.

`middle` has two tail-call-site candidates (both are `Item::Call` stmts
whose results are combined with `+`, not raw tail-calls, but the propagated
scan walks all `Item::Call` stmts): `inner_a` is `Some(2)` -> propagated
`Some(1)`; `inner_b` is `Some(1)` -> propagated `Some(0)`.
`frames!(call_sites => map:.., max).flatten()` picks `Some(1)` -- the
*maximum* across both sites -- so `is_inlinable(middle) = Some(1)`.

`outer` calls `middle` (depth 1 -> inline). Inside inlined `middle`,
`inner_a` (depth 2 -> inline) and `inner_b` (depth 1 -> inline) are both
inlined. Final computation: `(a + b) + (a * b)` = `(3 + 4) + (3 * 4)` =
`7 + 12` = `19.0`.

With the old short-circuit-on-first logic this test would be
order-dependent and could fail if `inner_b` was visited first. The `max`
ensures the *best* depth is always selected regardless of CFG iteration
order.

No `cps`/`cps_c`/`native_c`/`cps_rust` variant here -- all four route
through the *legacy* `ContinuationConverter::conv` (`run_cps_func`/
`run_cps_c_func`/`run_native_func_c`/`compile_cps_func` all still call
`fast_func_to_cps`, not the drive path -- `cps_c`/`native_c` additionally
run `extract_native_funcs` afterward, but that's downstream of the same
conversion), which panics converting this specific two-inlined-callee
shape: `Vec::drain` with an out-of-range end index at `to_cps/fast.rs:674`,
discovered by this test. Not investigated further since that path is
slated for removal in favor of `drive` (see `fast_func_to_cps_drive`)
rather than fixed -- a genuine legacy-path bug, not a MiniBC coverage gap.

(`e2e_inlineme`/`e2e_inlineme_n`/`_param_depth`/`_stmt_call` -- the
single-callee siblings of this family -- DO get full `cps`/`cps_c`/
`native_c`/`cps_rust` coverage: their simpler one-inlined-callee shape
doesn't trip the legacy converter's bug, and `cps_c`/`native_c` needed a
separate `extract_native_funcs` fix -- see `resolve_call_shape` and
`chained_dedup_never_merges_different_external_targets` in
dreamcompiler-cps/src/native_funcs.rs -- before those passed too.)

cases.name: and_bare_param_cond_true
cases.module: export function and_bare_param_cond_true(cond) { return cond && 1.0; }
cases.note:
Regression for a MiniBC-family register-allocator bug: a Fast IR block
whose own `FastTerm::Cond`/join-block pattern conditions on (or forwards)
a value that is itself an *unused-before-the-branch* param/prior value of
that same defining block, where the "then"/"else" targets are argument-
less trampoline blocks referencing operands by their original `FastValId`
rather than as explicit jump args. `lower_func`'s "inherited values"
cross-block mechanism (`dreamcompiler-mini-target/src/lower/mod.rs`) pins
such a value to a fixed register for the whole function, but two things
in `lower_block` (`.../lower/block.rs`) didn't know about that pin:
the per-stmt dead-code elimination (a "pure" stmt like a numeric literal
with zero *local* uses got skipped entirely, even though another block
needed it), and result-register assignment (even once not skipped, a
fresh register was assigned instead of the pre-reserved inherited one).
Both are fixed at the allocator level; this and the sibling ternary
family below are regression anchors for both the `&&`/`||` short-circuit
arm and the ternary `Item::Select` arm in `to_fast_ir/js.rs`, which share
the exact join-block shape that triggers this.

cases.name: weakmap_native_intrinsic
cases.module:
import { weakSet, weakGet, weakHas } from "~weakmap";
export function weakmap_native_intrinsic(a, b) { const k1 = {}; const k2 = {}; weakSet(0, k1, a); weakSet(0, k2, b); return weakGet(0, k1) + weakGet(0, k2) + (weakHas(0, k2) ? 1 : 0) - 1; }

emulation table, and no table-to-key strong edge is created.

export function weakSet(wm, key, value) { wm.set(key, value); }
export function weakGet(wm, key) { return wm.get(key); }

cases.note:
Collection parity (#32), native tier: two tables (handle 0 and 1) with the
same key object stay isolated.

cases.name: reflect_trap_mirror
cases.module: export function reflect_trap_mirror(a, b) { const t = { y: b }; const p = new Proxy(t, { get(tt, k) { if (k === "x") { return a; } return tt.y; }, has(tt, k) { return k === "w"; }, deleteProperty(tt, k) { return true; } }); return Reflect.get(p, "x") + Reflect.get(p, "y") + (Reflect.has(p, "w") ? 1 : 0) + (Reflect.deleteProperty(p, "y") ? 8 : 0); }
cases.note:
Reflect parity (#35): each Reflect operation on a proxy fires the
corresponding trap — get/set/has/deleteProperty — and untrapped operations
forward to the target.

cases.name: reflect_apply_construct
cases.module: export function reflect_apply_construct(a, b) { function P(x) { this.x = x; } P.prototype = { get() { return this.x; } }; const p = new Proxy(function(x) { return x * 2; }, { apply(t, thisArg, args) { return t(args[0]) + 1; } }); return Reflect.apply(p, null, [a]) + Reflect.construct(P, [b]).get(); }
cases.note:
Reflect parity (#35): Reflect.apply fires the apply trap on a proxied
function; Reflect.construct builds an ordinary instance with prototype
wiring.
